channel.title: Writing - Mohamed Kadri
channel.description: Practical, tool-agnostic guides on AI-assisted engineering and running real production systems with small teams.

item.title: Five Thousand Alarms, One Ticket: Inside Alarm Correlation
item.description: One fiber cut, five thousand alarms, one ticket: every stage of alarm correlation, the demarcation rules, and the arrival-order problem that splits incidents.

item.title: The Map Is the Product: Rebuilding Network Topology
item.description: How a multi-vendor assurance platform reconstructs network topology from raw exports, why alarm correlation depends on that map, and the five places it breaks.

item.title: I Self-Hosted AI for a Week. The Model Was the Easy Part.
item.description: One week, one cloud GPU, a shelf of open models - and the discovery that the model is only one layer of an engineered system. Quantization, the 32B wall, the harness lesson, guardrails, and real GCP prices.

item.title: Your Cell Network Is Learning to See: ISAC, Explained by a Telecom Engineer
item.description: Cell towers as sensors: what 5G ISAC really does today, how big the wireless foundation models actually are, and the sensing business nobody has built.

item.title: Mixture of Experts (MoE) Explained Simply: Kimi K3 Has 2.8 Trillion Parameters and Uses 104 Billion
item.description: A zero-background guide to Mixture of Experts: experts, routers, total vs active parameters, and why a 2.8 trillion parameter model activates only 104 billion per word.

item.title: Why Long Context Is Hard: the KV Cache, MLA, and Kimi Delta Attention, Explained Simply
item.description: Part 2 of a zero-background series: why the memory of a long conversation is the hidden cost of AI, and the fixes - GQA, MLA and KDA - explained simply.

item.title: The Loop Meets the Microwave Network
item.description: What an agentic AI closed loop must actually reason about on microwave backhaul: rain fade vs hardware ambiguity, multi-vendor OSS islands, blast-radius-gated actions, and verification - with an open live demo.

item.title: Your AI Agents Need a NOC
item.description: What thirty years of telecom network-operations discipline transfers to AI agent fleets, what breaks in translation, and the assurance-tooling gap nobody has closed.

item.title: Who Operates the Operators? Running a Fleet of AI Agents Without Getting Paged at 3am
item.description: A field guide to applying the SRE incident loop to autonomous AI agents themselves: detection, a control plane, and a circuit breaker that keeps autonomy from making incidents worse.

item.title: One Repository, One Shared Brain: A Practical Guide to Shared AI Memory for Development Teams
item.description: A step-by-step, tool-agnostic guide to giving every developer and every AI coding agent on a team the same project memory.
